---
title: "Principles of good data visualization"
---

1. **[Look at your data](1-look-at-your-data.qmd)**
   - Problems and/or quirks with the data are easily ascertained
   - Modeling strategies often become clear only after examining the data
2. **[Use graph types people read accurately](2-graph-types.qmd)**
   - Angles and areas are difficult to judge accurately; a common scale is necessary to compare across groups
   - Bar charts and dot plots are among the most effective tools for comparing amounts across groups
3. **[Maximize the data-ink ratio, within reason (maybe)](3-data-ink-ratio.qmd)**
   - All aspects of the graph should aid in presenting the data
   - My less strict rule: all color should convey some information
4. **[Show uncertainty](4-uncertainty.qmd)**
   - Confidence intervals and standard errors should be included for model estimates / predictions
   - Be clear in your graph and/or text whether CIs or SEs are being plotted
5. **[Make groups easy to tell apart](5-groups.qmd)**
   - A legend should clearly delineate between the groups or data should be labeled directly
   - The colors and/or symbols on the graph should clearly delineate between different lines/groups
6. **[Choose axes that fit the data](6-axes.qmd)**
   - The "ticks" and gaps on the axes should be clear and logical
   - The y-axis (and usually the x-axis as well) should cover at least the 10th to the 90th percentile of observed values
7. **[Design for your audience](7-audience.qmd)**
   - All graphs should have a descriptive, informative title and substantive axis labels
   - Talks: the font in the graph should be large enough to be easily read from afar
8. **[Use graphs, not tables, for model results](8-model-results.qmd)**
   - Talks: keep your audience awake (and aid more rapid interpretation): use graphics whenever possible
   - Coefficient plots are very effective for replacing regression tables
9. **[Show what the model predicts](9-predictions.qmd)**
   - The most effective way to understand a model is almost always to examine what the model predicts
   - Do not connect predictions for nominal IVs with lines
10. **[Don't assume linearity](10-linearity.qmd)**
    - Examine the functional form of the relationship between your predictor and your outcome before you fit a model
